messages:
alex: Quick thread — I sketched a proposal for a tenant penalty decay + smoothing approach to reduce noisy-neighbor blasts without punishing steady-but-bursty customers. TL;DR: exponential decay on penalty score + short-term burst budget. Feedback?

maria: Curious to see the math. Do you mean we keep a per-org penalty value p(t) that decays and increases on detections? :thinking: 

alex: Exactly. Basic idea: maintain two counters per org: a rolling token_rate (tokens/sec over short window) and a penalty_score. On detection (rate > threshold * baseline) increment penalty_score by penalty_delta. Every second penalty_score *= decay_alpha (0 < alpha < 1). Effective allowed burst = base_burst * (1 - clamp(penalty_score, 0, 1)). So higher penalty reduces burst headroom.

jordan: That seems reasonable. How do we define baseline? per-key 95th percentile from last 24h? per-org median?

alex: Plan: baseline = max(min_baseline, org_95th_last_24h). Rationale: median too low for legitimate spikes; 95th gives some headroom. We also store short-term expected percentile to avoid stale baselines.

taylor: What about an org that does sudden legitimate large jobs (batch ingest)? We should allow a path to temporary uplift (support-requested bypass) and a cooldown.

alex: Agreed. We'll expose an admin API to set temporary_override with expiry and audit logs. Also recommend a telemetry tag so Console shows "override" and reason.

maria: Can you post the rough config knobs you'd want in quota-service? That helps SRE review impact.

alex: Sure — draft config snippet:

```yaml
quota_policy_version: v2
per_org:
  baseline_percentile: 95
  baseline_window_hours: 24
  min_baseline_tokens_per_sec: 5
  base_burst_tokens: 500
  penalty:
    increment_on_violation: 0.18   # add to penalty_score
    decay_alpha_per_sec: 0.98    # multiply penalty_score each sec
    max_penalty: 1.0
  detection:
    sensitivity_multiplier: 3.0  # rate > sensitivity_multiplier * baseline triggers violation
    short_window_sec: 15
    long_window_sec: 300
  cooldown:
    override_expiry_sec: 86400
    auto_cooldown_sec: 3600
```

jordan: Real question: how do we surface this in metrics so product can see who is being penalised? We need a per-org timeseries of penalty_score, violations/sec, burst_shrink_pct.

alex: Yes, we plan to emit: org.penalty_score, org.violation_count_short_window, org.baseline_tokens_per_sec, org.effective_burst_tokens. Also expose histograms for latency changes when penalty > 0 (to watch for regressions).

maria: For rollout, we should A/B test on non-critical regions. Suggest two-minute canary per org group: group A uses current limiter, group B uses smoothing with very low increment value. Then gradually increase increment_on_violation.

alex: Proposed rollout: 1) internal-only 48h heavy-sim tests (replay production traces), 2) 1% traffic canary (low penalty), 3) 10% for 24h, 4) global. We'll gate by no more than 0.5% increase in 99p latency and <0.1% of requests getting 429 unexpectedly.

quota-bot: new-issue created: "tenant-penalty-decay: rollout plan + metrics" (#4521)

taylor: Implementation note: make penalty_score floats, but persist with low-cost encoding (1 byte mantissa) in redis to avoid big memory blowups. We should also sharded-lru the per-org state for low-usage tenants.

maria: Edge-case: multiple API keys per org. We should compute penalty at org level but surface key-level breakdowns. Otherwise a noisy key could take down everyone.

alex: Yeah, detection will increment org penalty; the UI will show key-level violation counts so we can ask customers to rotate or throttle specific keys. We'll also consider automatic key-level micro-throttles as a follow-up.

jordan: How about fairness between big and small tenants? If big tenants have huge baseline, burst still gives them advantage. Do we want a cap on absolute burst tokens to limit tail risk?

alex: Good call. Add global absolute_burst_cap: 10k tokens for now. Also a per-org soft_boost for enterprise SKUs (in account metadata) so sales can opt-in.

maria: Can you add a short experiment matrix in the PR? Looking for these outcomes: fewer 429s overall, fewer repeated violations from same org, stable latency percentiles, and lower impact on small orgs.

alex: Will add. Also adding a logging note: increment events should sample 1% of payloads with full headers for offline analysis.

taylor: One last thought: we need dashboard widgets: penalty heatmap (orgs on Y axis, penalty_score color), top N violators table, and a per-org timeline with annotations for overrides. Ops should be able to trigger a temporary lift from Console.

alex: I'll wire up Grafana panels in the PR and a Console flag in the UI mock. Thanks for the feedback — I'll open the RFC and link to the simulation results. :thumbsup: 

jordan: :shipit:
